title: Overview Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · 15 October 2026 · code stays closed until you approve

short.lead: This is how the Overview screen, the piece you chose to build first, gets built: four steps, each a GitHub issue under the parent issue Life overview (#6). It reuses the Board screen's pattern, so it adds two new code files and touches four existing ones. Three small choices are left for you.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it builds and how it is checked.
items: Step 1: work out the week and the areas (issue #10)

A file of plain calculations with no screen code, app/js/overview.js. It sorts open tasks into seven days starting today, puts overdue tasks on today, and totals the tasks in each life area. It has unit tests for due today, overdue, done, undated, no area, and a week crossing a month end.
Step 2: add the screen to the rail (issue #11)

The Overview screen itself: an Overview button in the rail and the phone bottom bar, the week strip, the area cards and the bottom strip. Taps only move you to existing screens; nothing on this screen changes your data. Both new files join the offline file list.

items.caption: The approved design this step builds.

items: Step 3: check it in a real browser (issue #12)

A script that opens the app in Chromium, a real browser, with realistic data: around 19 projects and 60 tasks. It tries desktop and phone widths, in light and dark. It checks that the page never scrolls sideways, that overdue tasks show on today in red, that taps work, and that the bottom bar fits five buttons. It runs twice in a row, and I look at its screenshots alongside the existing screens' screenshots from before the change.
The systems doc rewritten against the real code, a README entry, and the project state and Today notes updated.
A pull request from my branch. It links to the Life overview issue (#6) but does not close it.
You open the screen on your phone and computer, then merge the pull request or tell me what to change.

choices: area
What counts as a life area on the cards?
A
A project category
Projects already carry a category set in Settings (Work, Personal and Learning by default, renamable). One card per category, plus a card for projects with none.
B
Each project
One card per project. Simple, but with around 19 projects the cards stop being a glance.
C
Task labels
One card per label such as Chore or Art. Labels describe the kind of work, not an area of life, and one task can carry several.
It groups projects the way you already sorted them, and the card count stays small.
strip
What should the yellow strip at the bottom show before the importer exists?
A
The Unsorted count, opening the Sort screen
It is useful straight away, and it becomes the imported-notes count once the importer ships.
B
Nothing until the importer ships
A cleaner first version, with one less thing on screen.
It gives the strip a job from day one, and swapping its source later changes one line.
week
Where should the week strip start?
A
Today, then the next six days
Always shows a full week ahead, with overdue tasks on today.
B
Monday to Sunday of this week
Matches a paper calendar, but by Friday most of the strip is in the past.
It always shows a full week ahead, and overdue tasks sit on today, where you will act on them.
